focus.label: Blaschkolinear verrucous nevus
focus.why: The pathologist's biopsy analysis directly corroborates this diagnosis: hyperkeratosis, acanthosis and papillomatosis with focal epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, perinuclear vacuolization and coarse keratohyaline granules are the characteristic histologic signature of an epidermolytic epidermal (Blaschkolinear verrucous) nevus. This, together with the existing bilaterally symmetrical verrucous plaques along Blaschko lines, early onset with seasonal variation, and normal hair/nails/oral/systemic findings, reinforces the diagnosis. Confidence rises from 0.85 to 0.93; only the unavailability of KRT1/KRT10 and family-history data prevents it from being higher.
